paper_metadata.title: An Ultra-Low-Power 9.8GHz Crystal-Less UWB Transceiver with Digital Baseband Integrated in 0.18µm BiCMOS

figures.label: Fig. 25
figures.caption: Figure 25.2.1: System block diagram of the entire crystal-less UWB radio.

references.sentence: The architecture for the IR-UWB radio is shown in Fig. 25.2.1.
The receiver uses the non-coherent, energy-detection architecture shown in Fig. 25.2.2.
To reduce both power and area, the radio includes a relaxation oscillator with a modified RC network and a single-ended hysteretic comparator for on-chip clocking (Fig. 25.2.3).
Transmitted pulses are generated by the combined VCO and PA shown in Fig. 25.2.4.
The pulse generator has a 4b tuning range of 1.2ns to 6.0ns, and when enabled, the TX delivers a 700mVpp pulse to a 50Ω load (Fig. 25.2.4).
The PSD of the TX is shown in Fig. 25.2.5.
The magnitude response of the RX, shown in Fig. 25.2.5, is tuned to 9.8GHz.
At a 10-3 BER, the RX has a sensitivity of -67dBm and a 30kb/s data rate while consuming an average of 37μW from a 3.6V supply with 6% duty-cycling (Fig. 25.2.5).
The CL has a 6-to-38μA tuning range (Fig. 25.2.5), which is sufficient for sustained operation of the TX and RX.
A complete performance summary is provided in Fig. 25.2.6.
The die occupies approximately 2.73mm2, dominated by the modem (Fig. 25.2.7).
